title: Yield a Session from Depends and close it
summary: Fix an exhausted QueuePool with a yield dependency, move commit and rollback into it, then stop swallowing the exception.

files.content:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import Item

engine = create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://app@localhost/app")
app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(item_id: int):
    session = Session(engine)
    item = session.get(Item, item_id)
    return {"id": item.id, "name": item.name}

from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Item(Base):
    __tablename__ = "items"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), unique=True)

turns.user: after a while everything dies with QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out. restart fixes it

assistant.body: Each request opens a Session and never closes it, so the connections never go back to the pool and it runs dry at 15. The FastAPI way is a dependency that yields the Session. Leaving the with block closes it, which guarantees the connection is returned. Wrapping the type in Annotated saves writing Depends on every endpoint.

turns.user: fixed. want a POST /items too. and do commit/rollback in the dependency, not writing that in every endpoint

assistant.body: Great, let's move it all into get_session. Commit goes after the yield, and an exception triggers a rollback. In other words, the endpoint only has to add and flush. The flush assigns the id, so it can be returned straight away.

turns.user: posting the same name twice gives a 500, fine, but the log never shows the IntegrityError. just some weird thing about Response not awaited and bare except

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous get_session swallowed the exception in its except block. A dependency with yield that catches an exception has to raise it again, and Response not awaited is FastAPI pointing at exactly that. This adds a raise right after the rollback.
